title: Explicitly review common service capabilities
goal: Prevent commonly applicable cross-cutting capabilities, especially identity and login, from disappearing between requirements discovery and first-version scope selection.
in_scope: Update the project-local requirements-interview skill to run an explicit applicability review of common cross-cutting capabilities after requirements review and before final feature mapping and MVP scope selection.

Offer a broader, non-exhaustive catalog of adaptable candidates: identity and access (login, anonymous access, roles, account lifecycle, user-data separation); data management (create/update/delete, import/export, bulk actions, history); discovery (search, filter, sort); workflows (assignment, approvals, status, collaboration); communication (notifications and preferences); administration and configuration; reporting and analytics; integrations; and operational or quality needs such as audit history, security, privacy, accessibility, localization, reliability, backup, and recovery.

For each relevant candidate, establish and record one disposition: needed in the first version, not needed with a brief rationale, deferred to a later version, or unresolved with a follow-up question.

When requirements refer to a user's own data, private records, or role-specific access, explicitly ask how the user will be identified and what access should be restricted; consider the selected identity/access capability as a prerequisite in the feature map when required.
Reflect confirmed decisions, deferrals, and unresolved questions in the functional/non-functional requirements documents and feature map before presenting MVP scope options.
Avoid assuming that login is required or unnecessary without an explicit product-context decision.
out_of_scope: Forcing every common capability into every product or first-version scope.
Selecting a particular authentication provider or implementing authentication.
acceptance_criteria: The skill has a distinct common-capability review before final feature mapping and MVP selection.
Login/identity and access control are explicitly resolved as first-version, not needed, deferred, or unresolved for applicable user-facing products.
User-specific, private, or role-specific requirements trigger targeted identity and access follow-up questions.

The skill offers examples across data management, discovery, workflows, communication, administration, reporting, integrations, and operational quality, and selects only relevant candidates for discussion.
Each relevant candidate receives a disposition without turning the example catalog into a compulsory checklist.
Decisions and open questions are recorded in the requirements documents and their required dependencies appear in the feature map.
The skill never assumes a login implementation or provider without user confirmation.
